bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: National University of Singapore
providers.description: The National University of Singapore (NUS) is Singapore's flagship public research university, ranked #8 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. NUS does not operate a single unified, public developer portal; its documented, programmatically accessible footprint is concentrated in its open scholarly infrastructure. The institutional repository ScholarBank@NUS runs on DSpace 7.6 and exposes both a REST API and an OAI-PMH metadata harvesting interface. Module and timetable data is also available via the community-maintained NUSMods API (unofficial), which normalizes NUS course information. Most administrative and student-facing systems sit behind ADFS/SAML single sign-on and are not publicly documented.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Advance Intelligence Group
providers.description: Advance Intelligence Group is an AI-driven technology company headquartered in Singapore, founded in 2016 and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Warburg Pincus and others. It operates three core business lines: ADVANCE.AI (Southeast Asia's leading provider of digital identity verification, KYC/KYB, AML, compliance and risk-management solutions, serving 500+ enterprise clients), Atome Financial (buy-now-pay-later and digital lending) and Ginee (e-commerce enablement). The ADVANCE.AI business unit exposes a public Open API for eKYC — token authentication, global document verification, OCR field extraction, face comparison and liveness detection — used across banking, fintech, payments, retail and e-commerce in emerging markets. This API Evangelist profile was enriched from the public developer documentation at doc.advance.ai.

providers.name: Nanyang Technological University
providers.description: Nanyang Technological University (NTU Singapore) is a public research university in Singapore and is ranked #15 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. NTU's public, machine-readable footprint is concentrated in its library and research infrastructure: DR-NTU (Data), a Dataverse-based open research data repository, exposes a documented HTTP API, and DR-NTU (Digital Repository of NTU), a DSpace 7 / DSpace-CRIS institutional repository, exposes a REST API and an OAI-PMH endpoint. Other institutional systems (student information, timetabling, mobile app backends, SSO) are present but not publicly documented as open APIs.

providers.name: Aspire
providers.description: Aspire is a Singapore-headquartered fintech offering an all-in-one finance platform for growing businesses operating globally. Its products include multi-currency business accounts, corporate cards, global payments and FX, expense and budget management, bill pay, bulk payments, invoice and accounts-receivable management, yield on idle balances, and global payroll. Aspire also exposes a developer API (api.aspireapp.com/public/v1) covering payouts/transfers, card issuance, and bank-feed/transaction reporting, secured with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens (client-credentials and authorization-code + PKCE flows), idempotency keys, and webhooks. The company serves 50,000+ businesses, is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, and is PCI DSS v4.0.1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and SOC 2 Type 2 certified.

providers.name: 2C2P
providers.description: 2C2P is a Singapore-headquartered payments platform serving merchants across Southeast Asia and beyond. Its Payment Gateway (PGW) API - currently Payment v4.3 - lets merchants accept cards, e-wallets, QR, installments, and alternative payment methods via a server-to-server REST interface where every request and response body is a JWT (JWS) signed with the merchant's secret key. The platform covers hosted-page and Secure Fields (direct) card capture, tokenization and recurring payments, transaction inquiry and status, void/cancel and refund maintenance, currency exchange, and backend (server-to-server) payment notifications. 2C2P is part of Ant International.

providers.name: Xfers
providers.description: Xfers is a Southeast Asian payments infrastructure company founded in Singapore in 2015 and backed by 500 Global, providing bank-transfer collection, payouts, escrow-style wallets, and lending disbursement APIs across Singapore and Indonesia. Xfers merged with Payfazz in 2022 to form the Fazz Financial Group, with its regulated Singapore dollar stablecoin and payments business continuing as StraitsX; the Xfers v3 API documentation for Singapore and Indonesia remains published at docs.xfers.io.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: Vauld
providers.description: Vauld (formerly Bank of Hodlers) is a crypto asset management platform founded in India and headquartered in Singapore, backed by Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Pantera Capital, and Coinbase Ventures. Its Enterprise API exposes wallets, INR fiat rails, KYC verification, crypto swaps, borrowing, and lending to partner organisations, authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 request signing. Vauld suspended customer withdrawals in July 2022 and entered creditor-protection restructuring in Singapore; the API documentation remains published and the platform API still responds, though the documented testnet hosts no longer resolve.

providers.name: Homage
providers.description: Homage is a Singapore-headquartered holistic health and caregiving platform that connects families with screened, professional caregivers, nurses, and therapists to deliver personal care, home nursing procedures, rehabilitation, and health services where people live. Founded in 2016, Homage operates across Singapore, Malaysia, and Australia through consumer mobile apps and a care-management operations platform, offering flexible on-demand and recurring visits, care assessments, custom care plans, and teleconsultations for conditions such as dementia, stroke recovery, and post-surgical care. Homage does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this profile captures its public web properties and probed domain security.

providers.name: Chi Longevity
providers.description: Chi Longevity is a Singapore-based longevity medicine and healthy-aging clinic that focuses on biological-age optimization rather than reactive medicine, built on The Maier Method developed by co-founder Professor Andrea Maier. The practice combines precision health mapping (blood panels, genetic and cognitive testing, cardiovascular and metabolic analysis), flagship and specialised longevity programmes, cognitive and physical training, a branded NMN supplement, and ongoing support through health coaching, physician and dietitian consultations, and a client portal. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile carries the company identity, domain-security posture, and published web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Singtel
providers.description: Singtel (Singapore Telecommunications Limited) is Singapore's largest mobile network operator and the anchor communications group of Southeast Asia, with a regional footprint that includes Optus in Australia and associate stakes in Airtel, AIS, Globe and Telkomsel. In the network-API value chain Singtel sits on the supply side: it owns the mobile network signals — SIM, line, device, location, call state — that the CAMARA specifications turn into callable APIs, and it packages them for Singapore as SingVerify, a five-API anti-fraud and identity suite built on the GSMA Open Gateway framework. It also operates Paragon, its own 5G/edge/network orchestration platform, which powers the Bridge Alliance API Exchange (BAEx) federating network APIs across Bridge Alliance member operators, and it is one of the twelve carrier equity partners in Aduna, the Ericsson-led joint venture that aggregates operator network APIs into a single global commercial channel. Its API posture, however, is partner-gated and sales-led: as of July 2026 there is no first-party developer portal (developer., developers., docs. and opengateway. subdomains do not resolve), no published OpenAPI, no sandbox, no SDKs and no self-serve signup. Every SingVerify and CPaaS API page on singtel.com terminates in an enterprise enquiry form, and the BAEx portal is an explicit login wall for approved partners. Developers reach Singtel's network capabilities through aggregators — Aduna and its platform partners (Vonage, Sinch, Infobip, Google Cloud), the Bridge Alliance exchange, or identity vendors such as IPification — rather than directly from Singtel. Two surfaces do exist and are captured here: www.singtel.com publishes a first-party llms.txt family (root plus consumer, support and corporate companion files, last updated 2026-06-30) that indexes its marketing and support estate for AI systems while naming none of its APIs, and Singtel runs a footer-linked vulnerability disclosure programme at vdp.singtel.com and on HackerOne. api.singtel.com is a live Apigee gateway behind Imperva that answers every unrouted path with an Apigee fault envelope — a real gateway with nothing publicly bound to it.

providers.name: Get
providers.description: Get (useget.com) is a Singapore-based fintech company offering a mobile banking and financial-literacy platform for children, teens, and their families. The Get app pairs separate kid and parent accounts with prepaid Visa cards, parental spending controls, automated weekly allowances, a chore-based reward system, real-time spending analytics, and savings-goal folders, so young people can practice using real money tools in a safe, supervised environment. Get sells consumer subscription tiers (Get Core and Get Plus) plus a family account, and operates under a Payment Services exemption in Singapore. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification is published at this time; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Youtrip
providers.description: YouTrip (You Technologies Group, you.co) is a Singapore-based fintech that operates a multi-currency mobile travel wallet paired with a prepaid Mastercard, letting consumers hold and spend in over 150 currencies with no foreign-exchange fees and competitive in-app exchange rates. Launched in 2018, the company also runs YouBiz, a business account and corporate card product for SMEs, and offers international transfers to more than 40 countries. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, YouTrip processes billions of dollars in transactions annually across Singapore, Thailand, and Australia. As of this enrichment pass YouTrip exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or GitHub organization; consumer-facing account access is available only indirectly through open-banking aggregators.

providers.name: Geniebook
providers.description: Geniebook is a Singapore-based educational technology company (Geniebook Pte Ltd, incorporated 2016) offering an AI-powered online learning platform for primary, secondary, and JC students. Its product suite includes GenieSmart (AI-personalised worksheets generated from a library of 300,000+ MOE syllabus-aligned questions, using algorithms co-developed with A*STAR), GenieClass (live and recorded online classes taught by experienced teachers), and GenieAsk (real-time moderated teacher chats for after-school academic support), plus a CAMPUS physical-tutoring offering and PSLE/JC preparation programmes. Geniebook serves more than 220,000 students across Singapore, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia, and is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. It is a consumer (B2C) learning application delivered via web and mobile apps; no public developer API is published.

providers.name: Propseller
providers.description: Propseller is a Singapore-based, technology-powered real estate brokerage founded in 2018 by Adrien Jorge. It helps property owners sell, buy, and rent residential real estate — HDB flats, condominiums, and landed homes — pairing top-performing human property agents with data and technology to deliver an end-to-end transaction experience at a transparent commission starting from 1%. Backed by Vertex Ventures and Partech, Propseller operates a consumer-facing real estate service and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or programmatic integration surface.

providers.name: Caresense Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: CareSense Pte. Ltd. (CareSense.ai) is a Singapore-based preventive digital health company building AI-powered health coaching. Its flagship product is Mandy, a 24/7 AI health coach delivered over chat and voice, paired with the CareSense.ai app — a personal health dashboard covering nutrition, exercise, sleep and stress — and integrated health services including blood testing and telemedicine. The company sells both to individuals and to enterprise teams as a workplace wellbeing programme. CareSense was incorporated in Singapore on 14 June 2024 (UEN 202424008M), registered at 160 Robinson Road #14-04, and was founded by Lucas Ngoo, co-founder of Carousell, and Julian Koo, founder of the home-care platform Jaga-Me. As of this enrichment pass CareSense publishes no public API, developer portal, API documentation or SDKs; its technology surface is consumer and enterprise applications fronted by a Vanta-hosted trust center.

providers.name: Prudential plc
providers.description: Prudential plc is a life and health insurance and asset management group incorporated in England and Wales and listed on the London, Hong Kong, Singapore and New York exchanges, with its principal operating office in Hong Kong and roots in London going back to 1848. Its home market for this profile is the United Kingdom, but its book is almost entirely Asian and African: life protection, health and medical, savings and retirement, takaful, pensions and Hong Kong Mandatory Provident Funds, plus asset management under the Eastspring brand, across Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Taiwan, India, mainland China, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and a dozen African markets including Kenya, Uganda, Ghana, Nigeria and Zambia. It is no longer a UK retail insurer at all - the UK and Europe business was demerged as M&G plc in 2019 and the US business as Jackson Financial in 2021 - so the familiar UK "Pru" brands at pru.co.uk belong to M&G, not to this company. Its API posture is that there is no public API posture. Prudential plc publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no downloadable OpenAPI or Swagger document and no partner integration surface of any kind: developer, developers, docs, api, apis, partners, portal and sandbox subdomains of prudentialplc.com all fail to resolve, and /developers, /api, /developer, /partners and /integrations on the corporate site all return HTTP 404. The group's stated technology strategy is inward-facing - AI, automation, cloud and a global AI Lab running over a hundred internal use cases - and its distribution is built on tied agency forces and exclusive bancassurance partnerships with banks such as Standard Chartered, CIMB, MSB, SeABank, Bank Syariah Indonesia and UOB, which are commercial and contractual relationships rather than published API programmes. The Pulse by Prudential health and wealth app onboards health-tech and wealth-tech partners (Babylon, Tictrac, Halodoc, Smarter Health, Prive Technologies, OVO, Google Cloud) but every announcement describes the arrangement in commercial terms and none exposes a developer programme, SDK or public API. No ACORD, AL3, ACORD XML or NGDS reference was found anywhere in Prudential plc's public estate. Recorded honestly as a large carrier with a fully partner-gated, non-public integration surface. One genuine machine-readable surface does exist, and it is not an API: six of the group's market operating companies - Prudential Hong Kong, Prudential Singapore, Prudential Indonesia, Prudential Vietnam, Pru Life UK in the Philippines and Prudential BSN Takaful in Malaysia - publish real first-party llms.txt documents for grounding large language models, with Prudential Vietnam declaring a per-user-agent bot access policy for gptbot, claudebot, google-extended, perplexitybot and six other crawlers. The corporate domain publishes none. Underneath that, the group runs a visibly centralised security posture: TLS 1.3 and HSTS on every market host, and one shared PowerDMARC/PowerSPF tenant with a common aggregate-report mailbox across all seven domains, at p=reject on the corporate domain and p=quarantine in the markets, with no CAA record anywhere.

providers.name: Zenyum
providers.description: Zenyum is a Singapore-founded, direct-to-consumer oral-care and dental company operating across Asia. Its flagship product is ZenyumClear invisible braces (clear aligners) delivered through a network of partner clinics, alongside a broader oral-care line that includes ZenyumSonic electric toothbrushes, ZenyumBright whitening strips, serums and pens, toothpastes, water flossers and floss. Zenyum sells online and through retail across Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and Japan, and is backed by venture investors including Partech. As of this profile the company operates consumer e-commerce and clinic-partner surfaces but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or GitHub organization; this record captures its verifiable public web and domain security footprint.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: BoxGreen
providers.description: BoxGreen (BoxGreen Pte. Ltd., incorporated 2014 in Singapore) is a Certified B Corporation and social enterprise selling all-natural, individually packaged healthy snacks direct to consumers and to businesses. Its consumer offering is a Shopify-based e-commerce store with build-your-own snack boxes, curated collections (nut mixes, crunchies, vegan and gluten-free ranges), gift and party packs, and a subscription delivery model; its B2B side covers corporate gifting, office pantry supply, and cashless healthy-snack vending machines. Every BoxGreen snack is packed in prison by beneficiaries of Singapore's Yellow Ribbon Project to build skills and employability. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company, BoxGreen publishes no first-party API or developer program; the only machine-readable surface on its domain is Shopify's New Customer Accounts OIDC/OAuth discovery.

providers.name: Horizon Quantum Computing
providers.description: Horizon Quantum Computing is a Singapore-based quantum software company founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons. It builds software infrastructure for quantum applications, centered on Triple Alpha, an integrated development environment that lets developers write hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction and deploy them to quantum processors. Triple Alpha's final workflow step packages a program and deploys it as an API so developers can invoke quantum backends from Python scripts, web pages, and other technologies. Horizon operates its own quantum computing testbed at its Singapore headquarters and supports a range of external quantum processors, aiming to bridge the gap between today's quantum hardware and real-world applications. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or client SDK; API-based program deployment is offered to early-access users of the Triple Alpha platform.

providers.name: Finbots.AI
providers.description: Finbots.AI (finbots.ai) is a Singapore-headquartered fintech offering CreditX, a no-code, AI-powered credit risk platform that lets banks and lenders build, validate, and deploy application, behavioural, and collection scorecards in hours instead of months. Its proprietary, explainable machine-learning models power real-time lending decisions in under 0.03 seconds, and the platform adds a Decision Engine (business rules), propensity modelling, and managed data services. Backed by Accel, finbots.ai serves retail banking, SME lending, and credit-card clients across APAC and MEA markets, and was among the first fintechs to complete Singapore's AI Verify AI-governance testing framework. No public self-service developer API is published; API integration is enterprise and sales-gated.

providers.name: Endowus
providers.description: Endowus is a Singapore- and Hong Kong-based digital wealth management platform founded in 2017 by Gregory Van and Samuel Rhee. It gives retail, accredited, and private-wealth clients access to low-fee institutional share-class funds, advised and self-directed portfolios, and private-market and alternatives strategies across Cash, CPF (Central Provident Fund), and SRS (Supplementary Retirement Scheme) accounts. Its conflict-free model rebates 100% of trailer fees and fund-manager commissions to clients. Endowus is licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (CMS License 101051), serves 300,000+ clients, and manages over US$10 billion in assets. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company operates consumer apps but publishes no public developer API or documentation at this time.

providers.name: VaultDragon
providers.description: VaultDragon (Vault Dragon Pte Ltd) is a Singapore-based digital healthcare company building end-to-end practice-management software for clinics and medical providers across Southeast Asia and China. Its product suite includes DragonHub, an end-to-end clinic-management platform covering appointment scheduling, patient tracking, electronic health records, inventory and invoicing; DragonCare, a patient-facing web app for self-booking, reminders and access to medical history; DragonInsights, an on-demand business- intelligence and analytics layer; and DragonLab, a laboratory information system automating the workflow from sample receipt to report delivery. VaultDragon serves 650+ healthcare providers across Singapore, China, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia. The platform is delivered as a hosted SaaS (hub.vaultdragon.com) backed by a private, authenticated internal API; the company currently publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or client SDKs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Apar Infotech Corporation
providers.description: Apar Infotech Corporation, which operates publicly as Apar Technologies, is a Singapore-headquartered IT services and consulting group serving clients across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and the Americas. The firm delivers technology consulting and application services, data management and business intelligence, collaboration and content management, enterprise applications, managed services, staff augmentation and collaborative development centres, with practice areas spanning artificial intelligence, cloud, CRM, ServiceNow workflow, RPA/BPM hyperautomation, enterprise mobility and IoT. Apar also publishes a small set of its own products — the Otomeyt HR technology and technical-assessment platform, the Innoculate IoT monitoring platform, and the eLite SIS and eLite BAM applications. Apar is part of the Apar Group and is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Apar publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or self-service sign-up; its API work is delivered inside client engagements rather than as a public product surface.

providers.name: 99.co
providers.description: 99.co (99 Group) is a Singapore-headquartered real estate technology company and one of the largest property marketplaces in Southeast Asia. Founded in 2014 by Darius Cheung, Yan Phun and Conor McLaughlin, it operates consumer property portals across Singapore and Indonesia, including 99.co and SRX.com.sg in Singapore and 99.co/id and Rumah123.com in Indonesia. The platform lets buyers, renters and agents search HDB resale flats, executive condos, condominiums, landed homes and new-launch projects for sale and rent, with map-based search, transaction data, agent directories, mortgage tools and nearby-amenity insights (MRT, schools, commute times). 99 Group is backed by investors including Sequoia Capital, 500 Global, Golden Gate Ventures, Quest Ventures and East Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; 99.co exposes consumer web products but publishes no first-party public developer API or portal at this time.

providers.name: Grain
providers.description: Grain is a Singapore-based online restaurant and catering company founded in 2013 that delivers freshly prepared, thoughtfully sourced meals across Singapore. Its products include Meals On Demand (same-day ready-to-eat delivery), wedding catering, event catering, gift cards, and the Grain Savers program, with MUIS Halal and ISO certifications. Grain was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub (500 Global among its early backers). As of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer web storefront but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, or other machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Una Brands
providers.description: Una Brands is a Singapore-headquartered, digital-age e-commerce house of brands that acquires and operates consumer e-commerce businesses across the APAC region, accelerating their growth with operational expertise and AI-led innovation from teams in Singapore, China, and Indonesia. The company publishes no public developer API, but its website ships an llms.txt and a live Wix Site MCP endpoint that lets AI agents retrieve business details, search products and services, book appointments, and start purchases.

providers.name: Terrascope
providers.description: Terrascope is a Singapore-headquartered climate-tech and sustainability software company building an enterprise carbon measurement, management, and decarbonization platform. Launched in 2022 after being incubated and spun out of Olam Group (a Temasek-linked Singapore agribusiness), and led by former Google and AWS executive Felipe Daguila, Terrascope serves large food, agriculture, retail, and manufacturing enterprises that need to quantify Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions across their operations, products, and supply chains. The platform centers on four core modules: Corporate Carbon Footprint (CCF) for organization-level inventories, Product Carbon Footprint (PCF) for product-level lifecycle emissions, Supplier Engagement for Scope 3 primary-data collection, and Climate Reporting for audit-ready disclosure. Terrascope's differentiator is its AI-assisted data ingestion layer (built on Amazon Bedrock) that reduces measurement cycles by roughly 80% versus manual baselines, intelligent emissions factor matching with FLAG (Forestry, Land, and Agriculture) breakdowns, data gap-filling claiming 92% accuracy versus supplier data, and a curated library of over 20,000 decarbonization best practices used to power what-if scenario modeling and ROI-ranked recommendations. The platform supports the GHG Protocol (including Land Sector and Removals guidance), SBTi FLAG, CDP (Terrascope is a CDP Gold Accredited software provider), TCFD, California SB253, and Australia's S2 climate disclosure regimes. Notable customers include Kellanova, Princes Group, iNova Pharmaceuticals, Mandai Wildlife Group, Olam Food Ingredients, Tetra Pak, Mitsubishi, Japan Tobacco, and Kagome. Investors include Olam Group and Plug and Play Tech Center. Terrascope is delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS — there is no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, or open-source release. The github.com/terrascope organization exists but has no public repositories, and docs.terrascope.com is not publicly resolvable. Integration with customer ERP, procurement, and energy systems is handled through bespoke implementation engagements rather than self-serve developer onboarding.

providers.name: MyCash
providers.description: MyCash (operated by IN REMIT PTE LTD, Singapore) is a mobile-only cross-border remittance service built for migrant workers. Through the MyCash Money mobile app, users send money home instantly, reload / top up mobile airtime, and pay bills across supported corridors without needing a traditional bank account. The service targets the unbanked and underbanked migrant population with low-cost digital money transfer and mobile financial services. As of this profile MyCash publishes a consumer mobile application and marketing site (inremit.co) but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile records the company's public web and security posture.

providers.name: SALARY HERO PTE. LTD
providers.description: Salary Hero is a Singapore-headquartered financial wellness and earned wage access (EWA) platform offered to employees through their employers. Its products include Salary on Demand (accessing earned wages before payday), budgeting and spending-tracking tools, savings accounts (a partnership with Dime offering 3% interest), and financial-literacy education covering debt management and investing. The service is delivered via iOS and Android apps and is provisioned by employers, integrating with existing payroll and HR systems. Salary Hero is a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found.

providers.name: Ocean Network Express
providers.description: Ocean Network Express (ONE) is a Singapore-headquartered global container liner shipping company formed in 2017 through the integration of the container shipping businesses of three Japanese carriers — Nippon Yusen Kaisha (NYK), Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), and Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K-Line) — with commercial operations launching on 1 April 2018. Operating under the magenta "ONE" brand and the Standard Carrier Alpha Code ONEY, the company runs a fleet exceeding 2,200,000 TEU across 165+ weekly service loops calling at 244+ ports worldwide, making it one of the largest ocean container carriers globally. ONE participates in THE Alliance vessel sharing agreement and offers reefer, dangerous goods, out-of-gauge, and project cargo services alongside standard dry container moves. Its customer-facing digital surface centers on the ONE eCommerce platform (ecomm.one-line.com), which provides cargo tracking, instant quotation via ONE QUOTE (powered by Descartes Kontainers), spot booking, shipping instructions, electronic bill of lading, ePayment, and demurrage/detention inquiry. A partner-facing developer portal exists at developers.one-line.com alongside EDI integration channels, but ONE does not publish a fully open, self-service OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source code at either the github.com/ocean-network-express or github.com/OceanNetworkExpress organizations (both exist with zero public repositories). Tracking, booking, and schedule integrations are most commonly accessed by shippers and BCOs through third-party aggregators (Vizion, Portcast, JSONCargo, Terminal49, Tradlinx) or via DCSA-conformant carrier APIs delivered under commercial agreement.

providers.name: Myhero
providers.description: TradeHero (operated by My Manisku Pte Ltd, Singapore) is a gamified virtual stock-trading and social-investing mobile app. Users start with 100,000 virtual dollars to practice trading risk-free across 28 stock exchanges and 10 currency pairs, follow and copy validated top traders, learn through a short-tutorial investing academy, and compete on cash-prize leaderboards backed by real-time market data. Founded by former Wall Street trading-platform and Electronic Arts mobile-gaming veterans, and backed by venture firms including 500 Global, KPCB China, and IPV Capital. The public surface is a consumer mobile app and marketing site; no developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: PolicyPal
providers.description: PolicyPal is a Singapore-based InsurTech and digital insurance broker founded in 2016 by Val Yap that lets consumers buy, understand, and organize their insurance policies from a mobile app using OCR and rule-based policy digitization. Backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), PayPal Incubation, and Startupbootcamp FinTech, it was the first startup to graduate from the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox and was acquired by Hong Kong's AMTD Digital in 2020. As of 2025 PolicyPal Pte. Ltd. and its entities (including PolicyPal Tech Pte. Ltd., Baoxianbaobao Pte. Ltd. and the ValueChampion brand) are no longer regulated by MAS, and the consumer website is undergoing a revamp. PolicyPal does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Hydroleap
providers.description: Hydroleap is a Singapore-based greentech company revolutionizing industrial water and wastewater treatment through proprietary electrochemical technology. Its chemical-free, modularized systems - electro-coagulation (HL-EC), electro-oxidation (HL-EO), and electro-oxidation for cooling towers (HL-EO-CT) - replace conventional chemical-intensive processes with automated, energy-efficient alternatives. Hydroleap serves data centers, palm oil mills, food and beverage production, pharmaceuticals manufacturing, and municipal wastewater operators, helping businesses cut operating costs, improve regulatory compliance, and reduce environmental impact. Backed by 500 Global, the company is profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a product and marketing website but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: DocDoc
providers.description: DocDoc is Asia's leading patient empowerment company, positioning itself as the patients' trusted medical advisor. With a network of more than 23,000 doctors under contract and extensive proprietary data on outcome, price, and experience, DocDoc helps patients find the highest quality care for their unique medical needs. Headquartered in Singapore and backed by 500 Global, the company operates across Asia connecting patients with doctors, clinics, and hospitals through a data-driven medical advisory platform. DocDoc is profiled in the API Evangelist network as a healthcare technology company; no public developer/API surface was discoverable during enrichment.

providers.name: Oddup
providers.description: Oddup (now operating as Oddup Markets) is a Singapore-based platform founded in 2015 by James Giancotti. It began as a data-driven startup-rating and intelligence service — a 500 Global portfolio company scoring startups and crypto projects — and has since pivoted to prediction markets, letting users trade on real-world outcomes across crypto, FX, indices, and commodities using a distinctive Yes / No / Maybe outcome model. The current product is a client-side single-page web application hosted on Vercel at oddup.app (and oddup.com). As of this enrichment pass the live site is geo-restricted (HTTP 451, x-blocked-country: US) and exposes no public developer, API, documentation, or .well-known surface — no OpenAPI, no API subdomains, and no published packages were discoverable. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and a domain-security probe only; it will be re-enriched if a public API surface appears.

providers.name: Spenmo
providers.description: Spenmo was a Singapore-based spend management platform for businesses, offering corporate Visa debit cards (physical and virtual), bill and invoice management with smart scanning, employee reimbursements and claims, and accounting integrations with Xero, NetSuite, QuickBooks and Jurnal. Operated by Digital Services SG Five Pte Ltd, it worked with MAS-licensed payment partners rather than providing regulated payment services directly. The company ceased operations on 14 August 2025 and permanently disabled customer access. No public API or developer program was ever published.

providers.name: Movel AI
providers.description: Movel AI is a Singapore-based robotics deployment software company, founded in 2016, that makes it faster and cheaper to get autonomous mobile robots up and running in real-world environments. Its platform pairs deep learning, sensor fusion, and probabilistic planning so robots can perceive their surroundings and plan tasks on their own. Core products are the Movel Fleet Management System (FMS) for real-time monitoring and control of multi-robot fleets and Movel RNS (Robotic Navigation System) for precise single-robot navigation of complex spaces, applied across logistics, manufacturing, construction, and healthcare. The company is backed by Silicon Solution Ventures, 500 Global, AviTech, SGInnovate, Seeds Capital, and Enterprise Singapore. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Movel AI publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Aliena
providers.description: Aliena is a Singapore-based space-technology company, incorporated in 2018, that designs and manufactures compact electric propulsion systems for small satellites. Its MUSIC plasma thruster line delivers high thrust-to-power ratios at very low power budgets with high specific impulse, enabling small satellites to operate and sustain very low Earth orbit (VLEO) for high-resolution remote sensing. Aliena is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a 500 Global portfolio lead.

providers.name: Bilimber Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Bilimber Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based private company (exempt private company limited by shares) incorporated on 2020-11-17, operating in research and experimental development on electronics. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (an early/seed-stage investor alongside a Hong Kong government program) and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public website, developer portal, documentation, or API surface -- the bilimber.com domain is currently unregistered and does not resolve -- so no first-party API artifacts could be searched, derived, or generated. This profile remains a lead awaiting a public API surface.

providers.name: ESPL
providers.description: ESPL (Esports Players League) is a Singapore-headquartered global esports tournament network and platform, founded in 2019, building an open, grassroots-focused ecosystem for amateur competitive gaming. It runs ESPL-branded online and on-ground tournaments across Asia, Europe, and the Americas with a mobile-first focus alongside PC and console titles, operated from its Singapore headquarters with regional offices in Cologne and Los Angeles. ESPL is a portfolio company of 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), which led its seed round in 2020. As of this enrichment pass ESPL publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its espl.co domain did not resolve (DNS SERVFAIL) at probe time; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Krosslinker
providers.description: Krosslinker (KrossLinker) is a Singapore-based deep-tech advanced-materials company that designs and manufactures silica aerogels — among the most insulating solids known — using a proprietary, water-based and scalable chemistry and manufacturing platform the company calls Aspire. Its product line spans Cryar super-insulating aerogel composite board, QuintAero ultra-light silica aerogel powder, KrossShield SR Pro aerogel-powered cooling paint, and a flexible aerogel blanket in development, serving cold-chain pharma and food packaging, building and construction passive cooling, and industrial insulation. Krosslinker operates from CleanTech III in Singapore and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a physical-materials manufacturer and publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web, product, and security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: NodeFlair
providers.description: NodeFlair is a Singapore-based technology career-transparency platform, founded in 2018 by Ethan Ang, that gives Asia's tech talent access to verified salary data, company reviews, tech-stack insights, benefits, and job listings across the APAC region. Salaries are verified against actual employee payslips, differentiating NodeFlair from other job boards, and the platform serves over 500,000 monthly visitors across eight Asian countries while helping companies hire tech talent. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment; the profile currently carries live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Rawsome Pte. Ltd.
providers.description: Rawsome Pte. Ltd. (trading as Rawsome Asia Beverages) is a Singapore-based producer and distributor of small-batch, handcrafted raw kombucha sold under the Wild Boocha brand. The company brews fermented tea beverages -- including Citrus Green, Strawberry Mint, and Harmony Adaptogenic flavors -- available in one-liter bottles and refillable mini kegs, and markets them as a functional wellness drink rich in probiotics, polyphenols, B vitamins, vitamin C, organic enzymes, and amino acids. Rawsome operates a direct-to-consumer e-commerce storefront (built on Odoo) and was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. This profile currently has no public API, developer portal, or developer documentation; it is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Upcode Academy
providers.description: UpCode Academy was a Singapore-based coding school offering short bootcamps and part-time courses (SQL, Python, Web Development with Ruby on Rails, Data Science, Computer Vision, IoT) taught by industry practitioners. Operated by 40 Tasks, a 500 Global portfolio company whose earlier product was the LOCO location-based search app at 40tasks.com. The company appears defunct - upcodeacademy.com serves a Cloudflare 522 dead-origin error (a bare default server page by December 2025) and 40tasks.com no longer resolves in DNS (domain-squatted since about 2023). No public API surface was found.

providers.name: WorkClass
providers.description: WorkClass is (or was) a Singapore-based job marketplace founded in 2020 that matched frontline and blue-collar workers with employers, promising placement within 24 hours via matching algorithms. Backed by 500 Global, Goodwater Capital, Antler, and Kistefos, it surfaced here as a 500 Global portfolio lead. As of July 2026 its primary domain workclass.co redirects to an unrelated UK website and workclass.com is parked for sale; no public API, developer portal, client packages, or GitHub organization were found.

providers.name: Call Levels
providers.description: Call Levels was a Singapore-based financial technology company, founded in 2014 by Cynthia Siantar and Daniel Chia, that built a real-time financial markets monitoring and price-alert service. Its consumer mobile app (iOS and Android) let retail investors set price "call levels" and receive real-time alerts across multiple asset classes including forex, commodities, indices and equities, serving 500,000+ investors globally. On the institutional side it offered an open API and a chatbot/portfolio-management framework marketed to banks and financial institutions for embedding market monitoring into legacy systems. The company was backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) via a pre-Series A round. As of this profile the primary domain (call-levels.com) resolves to a parked registrar lander with no live developer portal, API documentation, or discoverable API surface, so the company appears dormant or defunct and no live API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Nugit
providers.description: Nugit is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Hillhouse Investment
providers.description: Hillhouse Investment (formerly Hillhouse Capital) is a global investment firm founded in 2005 by Lei Zhang with seed capital from the Yale University endowment, and is one of Asia's largest private-market investors, managing an estimated US$100 billion in assets as of 2026. Headquartered in Singapore with offices in Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, New York, London, and Abu Dhabi, the firm invests globally across all stages of a company's life cycle, spanning public equities, growth equity, private equity buyouts, venture capital (through its early-stage arm GL Ventures, launched in 2020), and real assets. Hillhouse describes itself as disciplined and pragmatic investors who prioritize business fundamentals and deep, bottom-up industry research, with sector focus on healthcare, industrials, energy transition, business services, and consumer. Its portfolio spans companies headquartered in more than 25 countries and has included category-defining businesses such as Tencent, JD.com, Baidu, Zoom, BeiGene, Miniso, Airbnb, Uber, and Didi. Backers have historically included major university endowments (Yale, Stanford, Princeton, MIT, University of Pennsylvania, University of Texas) and CPPIB.
